title: Segment tree: build and range sum query
summary: Each node stores the sum of a range; a query adds the few nodes that exactly cover the asked range.
note: Each query is [l, r] with l ≤ r: the sum of positions l to r, inclusive.

panels.label: tree (index = node; node k's children are 2k and 2k+1)

narration.text: There are {n} values.
The tree lives in a flat array. Each node's children sit at double its index and double plus one.
Define build: each node will store the sum of its range of positions.
Node {node} covers just position {lo}: it's a leaf.
Node {node} covers positions {lo} to {hi}: split it in two.
The leaf holds {tree[node]}.
Back up to the parent.
The halves split after position {mid}.
The left half, positions {lo} to {mid}, is built.
The right half, positions {mid + 1} to {hi}, is built.
Node {node} is the sum of its two children: {tree[node]}.
Define query: add up the nodes that exactly cover the asked range.
Node {node} covers {lo} to {hi}, outside the query {l} to {r}: it adds nothing.
Node {node} covers {lo} to {hi}, which overlaps the query {l} to {r}.
Return an empty sum.
Positions {lo} to {hi} lie entirely inside the query: use this node's sum, {tree[node]}, without going deeper.
Only part of {lo} to {hi} is inside the query: ask both children.
Return {tree[node]}.
The children split after position {mid}.
Add the two children's answers.
The tree is built. The root, node one, holds the total: {tree[1]}.
Answer the query {l} to {r}.
Every query is answered.
